section_entries.mathematical_role: Recasts moment bounds as analytic-continuation statements, gives a convolution recurrence, and uses the framework to argue heuristic optimality of the spectral conjecture.

unit_result_entry.title: Products of zeta moments induce a convolution recurrence among Z_k
unit_result_entry.why_material: Double Mellin inversion expresses a 2(k+l)-th moment through Z_k and Z_l with frequency coupling, while the modified-transform convolution lemma gives a direct recurrence Z_{k+l} as a vertical convolution. This suggests building higher-moment information compositionally from lower transforms.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Z₁ satisfies the conjectured mean-square scale but not the pointwise analogue
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The k=1 transform already has the mean-square exponent conjectured for Z₂ and a dyadic refinement, yet its Lindelöf-type pointwise bound remains out of reach. This demonstrates that mean-square success does not automatically resolve pointwise control even in the simpler case.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The eighth moment heuristically forces Conjecture 3’s square-root scale
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Taking k=l=2 in the transform factorization and isolating the discrete spectral contribution turns the known eighth-moment lower scale into a lower bound for a supremum of the same short oscillatory Hecke sums. After truncation and Stirling analysis, this argues that Conjecture 3 would be essentially optimal.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The convolution law makes Z_{k+l} compositional in Z_k and Z_l, while localized inversion reveals coupled spectral frequencies; this lets low-order transform information diagnose both higher moments and the plausible optimal scale of spectral cancellation.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Convergence contours and pointwise inputs are essential, and the final optimality argument is explicitly heuristic.
